doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First New York gigs: alto versus tenor, Dud Bascomb, Chicken Shack
summary: Told alto players could not work, he sat in around town, then played club shows and with Dud Bascomb at the Chicken Shack in Jersey.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you’re going to music school, and I assume that you start to make the rounds and establish contacts.
Let’s go into some detail about that. Who some of the first people were that you played with, and...

Well, the funniest thing about it, when I got there and I got to playing, and the guys said, “Yeah, man, you play good, but you’d better get a tenor, because alto players can’t work in New York.” I said, “Oh, no?” So one night I took my alto, I went around to every club on ‘25th Street and down on ‘16th Street, and I sat in with all the bands, and I came back the next day and I was laughing. They said, “Why are you laughing?” I said, “I don’t know whether it’s alto or tenor, but any job there I can get, because the guys there can’t play anything.”

Well, that’s just the way they talked. “You’ve got to play tenor.” Because then, see, everybody was walking the bar, playing “Flying Home” and stuff like that. But I got to working with a club where they had singers.

The Top Club, and some gigs at the Baby Grand, and some gigs at Smalls Paradise. They used to have entertainers. I got to playing in these clubs, and eventually I got to working with Dud Bascomb’s band, the trumpet player with Erskine Hawkins. He got a band, and we started working out in New Jersey, not too far from the prison out there, at a place called the Chicken Shack.
In Jersey. That was my regular gig, I could play that, but I could take off any time I wanted to if I got another gig. I was set up pretty good.
So you were interested in bebop, but on these gigs you weren’t playing bebop.
Yeah, I played bebop when I took a solo. I played the music, but I played bebop when I took a solo.
